passages.text: If someone should wish to say that what comes through predictions of this kind is like truly innate foreknowledge, he is greatly deceived. Such things disclose only what is present, and even that only if they speak truly. In another way, however, they too are useful to me, for they establish that foreknowledge exists. But the foreknowledge of the sole and true one knows not only the present; it extends prophecy without limit as far as the coming age itself, and needs nothing for understanding. He does not prophesy obscure and ambiguous things so as to make what is said require another prophet for understanding, but explicit and plain things, just as our teacher, being also a prophet, knew everything at all times through an innate and ever-flowing spirit.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν διὰ τῶν τοιούτων προρρήσεων τῇ ὄντως ἐνφύτῳ προγνώσει ὁμοίαν εἶναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: what comes through predictions of this kind is like truly innate foreknowledge
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first feminine article implies the foreknowledge claimed through such predictions. What comes through predictions represents that understood object without treating predictions themselves as the same thing as innate foreknowledge.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ δὲ τοῦ μόνου καὶ ἀληθοῦς πρόγνωσις
lexical_decisions.chosen: the foreknowledge of the sole and true one
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine substantivized adjectives identify a person, contextually the true prophet, whose foreknowledge is distinguished from the other predictions. The main text does not supply God as a uniquely established referent, and retains both sole and true.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ προφητεύων ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: He does not prophesy obscure and ambiguous things so as to make what is said require another prophet for understanding
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine nominative participle does not agree with feminine foreknowledge; it is read as resuming the person described by the genitive sole and true one, with a loose shift of construction. The later teacher-prophet is another possible contextual identification of that person. The negative governs obscure prophecy with its resulting need for another interpreter, not the existence of prophecy itself. No change to the selected Greek's case or gender is supplied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐνφύτῳ καὶ ἀεννάῳ πνεύματι
lexical_decisions.chosen: through an innate and ever-flowing spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both adjectives describe the spirit through which the teacher knows. Ever-flowing preserves the continuous-flow image rather than replacing it simply with eternal or intermittent inspiration.

source_issues.issue: The former Lagarde reading is exactly καὶ προφητειῶν. The selected reading μὴ προφητεύων is independently read from Dressel's 1853 main print. Dressel's apparatus attributes μὴ to Davisius: this is an editorial reading, not a newly collated manuscript or proof of uniquely recovered original wording. The selected negative and participle are translated, while their loose personal referent is disclosed separately.

passages.text: Copy of a letter to Apion, supposedly from the beloved woman. I am amazed that, after praising me for wisdom, you write to me as though I were foolish. For, wishing to persuade me into your passion, you drew your examples from myths about the gods, not afraid to blaspheme Love—the oldest of all, as you said, and above all gods and humans—so that you might corrupt my soul and outrage my body. For the love involved in desires is not the originator of the gods. If he desires willingly, he himself is his own passion and punishment, and one who suffers willingly would not be a god. But if he unwillingly desires union and, passing through our souls, is carried through our bodies as through instruments into unions with intelligible beings, the one who makes him love and carries him is greater than he is. And again, if that very one who carries him is carried by another longing, another, greater one is found who carries that one, and an endless regress of lovers results, which is impossible. Thus there is neither one who carries nor one who is carried; rather, it is the lover's own desiring passion, increasing through hope and diminishing through despair.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Ἀντίγραφον ἐπιστολῆς πρὸς Ἀππίωνα ὡς παρὰ τῆς ἐρωμένης
lexical_decisions.chosen: Copy of a letter to Apion, supposedly from the beloved woman
lexical_decisions.rationale: The heading's supposedly marks the letter's presented rather than certified authorship. It is retained without turning the heading into an authentic attribution.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔρωτα τὸν πάντων πρεσβύτατον (ὡς ἔφης) ἐπὶ πάντων θεῶν καὶ ἀνθρώπων
lexical_decisions.chosen: Love—the oldest of all, as you said, and above all gods and humans
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected ἐπὶ with the genitive is read as a relation of superiority, above or over all, describing Love alongside oldest of all. English and links the two descriptors without supplying a Greek participle meaning set or place. A material alternative attaches the prepositional phrase to blaspheme: before or in the presence of all gods and humans. The age and universal scope are retained in either reading; the superiority interpretation fits the ensuing denial that desire-based love originates the gods but is not claimed as uniquely established.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔρως γὰρ θεῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀρχηγέτης ὁ ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις
lexical_decisions.chosen: For the love involved in desires is not the originator of the gods
lexical_decisions.rationale: The qualification limits this denial to love associated with desires. Originator preserves the founding or originating force of ἀρχηγέτης; leader is a viable alternative stressing rule rather than origin.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὰς τῶν νοητῶν φέρεται συνουσίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: is carried ... into unions with intelligible beings
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied adjective concerns beings or things apprehensible to thought. With intelligible beings takes the genitive as partners of union; unions of intelligible beings is a material alternative leaving their relation broader. The unusual wording is not silently replaced with mortal or bodily partners.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς ἀπέραντον ἐπαναφορὰ τῶν ἐρώντων γίνεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: an endless regress of lovers results
lexical_decisions.rationale: The argument repeatedly seeks a greater bearer behind each bearer. Regress denotes that unending backward sequence rather than a finite recurring cycle.

source_issues.issue: The former Lagarde phrase is exactly ἐπὶ τῆς πάντων θεῶν καὶ ἀνθρώπων. The selected phrase ἐπὶ πάντων θεῶν καὶ ἀνθρώπων is Dressel's independently image-read main print, not a newly collated manuscript. It is not the separate marginal proposal ἐπιθεὶς, and no participle from that proposal has been adopted or silently added. The main interpretation and its alternative attachment are explained in the lexical note; no unique original wording is claimed.

passages.text: From their illegitimate union, illegitimate human beings came into existence, much taller than humans. Those who came afterward called them giants. They were not snake-footed beings who had raised war against God, as the blasphemous Greek myths sing, but beastlike in character, larger in size than humans because they came from angels, yet smaller than angels because they had been born of women. God knew that they had grown savagely beastlike and that the world was not sufficient to satisfy them, for it had been created in proportion to humans and for human use. So, lest through lack of food they turn to the unnatural eating of animals and seem free from responsibility, as though having dared this from necessity, almighty God rained manna upon them in response to their varied desire, and they enjoyed whatever they wished. But because of their illegitimate nature they were not pleased with the purity of the food and longed only for the taste of blood. That is why they were also the first to taste flesh.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς νόθου μίξεως αὐτῶν ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο νόθοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: From their illegitimate union, illegitimate human beings came into existence
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated adjective is preserved in both union and offspring. Hybrid or mixed-lineage captures a material aspect of the angel-human parentage, while illegitimate retains the ancient author's evaluative designation; it is not a modern legal or medical classification supplied by the translator.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολλῷ γε τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ κορυφὴν μείζους
lexical_decisions.chosen: much taller than humans
lexical_decisions.rationale: The head or crown phrase identifies the comparison as height or stature. It does not specify a fixed difference of exactly one head; the considerable difference expressed by πολλῷ is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ δρακοντόποδες ὄντες καὶ πρὸς θεὸν πόλεμον ἀράμενοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: They were not snake-footed beings who had raised war against God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The negative rejects the combined mythic characterization. The unusual snake-footed form is preserved rather than converted into an unnamed species or omitted.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μάννα αὐτοῖς ὁ παντοδύναμος θεὸς ἐπώμβρισεν ἐκ ποικίλης ἐπιθυμίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: almighty God rained manna upon them in response to their varied desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase from varied desire is read causally as responding to their differing desires, supported by their immediately ensuing enjoyment of whatever they wished. A more literal alternative is rained manna upon them from varied desire, which leaves whose desire it is broader. The main text does not specify flavors or turn manna into animal flesh.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μόνης τῆς τῶν αἱμάτων γεύσεως ἐγλίχοντο
lexical_decisions.chosen: longed only for the taste of blood
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected finite verb denotes craving or longing, with only governing the taste desired. The plural bloods is rendered idiomatically as blood without introducing separate victims or an act not supplied here.

source_issues.issue: The former Lagarde reading is exactly ἐγλίχοντα. The selected independently image-read Dressel main-print reading is ἐγλίχοντο, a finite verb translated longed. This is a documented print-variant choice, not personal manuscript collation or recovery of an autograph.

The selected text retains a full stop between eating and the participle turning. The English follows their surviving grammatical relationship as one construction. The point is not treated as an established lacuna, and no missing wording is supplied.

passages.text: For just as fearsome snakes draw sparrows to themselves by their breath, so these beings draw those who share their table toward their own will, having mingled with their minds through food and drink. In dreams they transform themselves according to the forms of carved images, in order to increase deception. For the carved image is neither alive nor possessed of a divine spirit; the demon that appeared made use of its form. To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams, and, when those people met one another while awake and compared what they had seen in dreams, did not agree? Thus that is no longer an apparition in a dream, but is either a demon's or the soul's, the soul reproducing as images the effects arising from present fears and desire. Or, indeed, struck by fear in its mind, it gives birth to images through dreams. If you think carved images, being possessed of breath, can perform such things, set them on a balance. With the beam level, place the counterweight on the other pan and ask them to become either heavier or lighter. If that happens, they have breath. But it does not happen. But if it does happen, is such a thing thereby a god? For this can happen even by a demon's finger. Worms move too, and are not called gods.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς αὐτῶν πνεύμασιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: by their breath
lexical_decisions.rationale: The snake comparison refers to breath or exhalation, not a separately named snake spirit. It is retained as the speaker's ancient analogy rather than corrected into modern animal behavior.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Thus that is no longer an apparition in a dream
lexical_decisions.rationale: The unusual form ἐπιφανείη is read nominally as apparition or manifestation with the expressed copula. A verbal optative reading might appear is morphologically possible but makes the copular sequence difficult. The clause is not expanded into an unexpressed adjective such as divine or genuine.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ψυχῆς τὰ ἐπιγενήματα τοῖς παροῦσι φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας
lexical_decisions.chosen: the soul's, the soul reproducing as images the effects arising from present fears and desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The effects and images are taken as two expressions of the dream products, with present fears and desire as the circumstances generating them. A material alternative foregrounds the returning of images in response to those fears and desire: the soul giving back images of their ensuing effects. The main text preserves both the effects and the images rather than collapsing the first accusative into the fears themselves. The selected present adjective directly agrees with fears, while desire is coordinated with them.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα
lexical_decisions.chosen: Or, indeed, struck by fear in its mind
lexical_decisions.rationale: The initial or is retained as another explanatory turn rather than silently deleted. The feminine participle continues the soul, and mind expresses the respect in which fear strikes it.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ ἔσται, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if it does happen, is such a thing thereby a god?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The next demon-finger and worm examples support a rhetorical question denying that movement alone establishes divinity. The source has a full stop, so the question punctuation is interpretive. An assertion such a thing is then a god is a formal alternative, but runs against the ensuing counterexamples; the Greek words have not been changed.

source_issues.issue: The former Lagarde reading is exactly παρίᾳ. The selected Dressel main-print reading παροῦσι was independently read from the primary image. Dressel's apparatus identifies it as Cotelerius's conjecture: its printed attestation is not a claim of directly newly attested manuscript wording. It is translated as present while the remaining sentence-level interpretation is separately disclosed; no unique original recovery is claimed.

passages.text: How many also falsely claim oracular responses and cures accomplished by these images, and confirm them with oaths? How many have hired themselves out, undertaking through certain contrivances to suffer something and proclaiming it in that way, then, having been restored from their affliction by a counteracting treatment, say that the cure was revealed by an oracle, so that they may label the unfeeling thing an object of worship? How many of these objects were consecrated from the beginning by magical art, so that they might dream and give oracles? Yet over a long time these too proved discordant. How many now practice sorcery, wishing to strengthen such things? Nevertheless, if something has powers of divination or healing, that does not make it a god.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτῶν τὸ πάθος ἀντιπαθείᾳ ἀποκατασταθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: having been restored from their affliction by a counteracting treatment
lexical_decisions.rationale: The restoration concerns the people in respect of their affliction, not a strengthening or restoration of the affliction itself. The counteraction opposes the contrived suffering; the text does not identify a substance, remedy, or procedure, so none is supplied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα τὸ ἀναίσθητον ἐπιγράψωσιν σέβασμα
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that they may label the unfeeling thing an object of worship
lexical_decisions.rationale: The insensate thing is what is labeled, and object of worship is its assigned designation. The translation does not add a physical inscription or a particular dedication text.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα ὀνειροπολῇ καὶ χρηματίζῃ
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that they might dream and give oracles
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected first verb concerns dreaming or dealing in dreams; the second concerns giving oracular responses. Dream preserves the lexical activity as attributed to the consecrated objects without inventing a mechanism. Deal in dreams or provide dream manifestations is a material contextual alternative in the preceding account of images appearing to dreamers. The source's singular verbs with the neuter plural things are rendered by normal English plural agreement.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μακρῷ χρόνῳ καὶ ταῦτα διεφώνησεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: over a long time these too proved discordant
lexical_decisions.rationale: The lack of agreement or consistency is retained, without inventing a specific prediction, date, or measurable error rate.

source_issues.issue: The former Lagarde reading is exactly ὑνερπολῇ. The selected independently image-read Dressel main-print reading is ὀνειροπολῇ, concerning dreaming or dream activity, not the unresolved former form. This is an explicitly documented public-domain primary-print variant; it is not adopted or relicensed upstream XML, a new manuscript collation, or an autograph claim. The contextual lexical alternatives remain disclosed.
